history.notes: A numeric property containing nan or inf (possible through a hand-edited project file) passed tonumber, defeated every range clamp (all nan comparisons are false), and could reach a timer interval or the wire. Numeric properties now fall back to their documented default when non-finite, and the transmit chokepoint refuses a non-finite value by name. · A non-finite Brightness could ship the literal body {"brightness":0} - a real dim-to-zero command the dealer never asked for. · Adds the fleet-standard Run Diagnostics and Run Self-Test dealer actions: read-only, license-independent, cached-state honesty. Diagnostics reports what the driver has already observed - never probing the network, never printing a secret. Self-Test proves the shared layer locally and ends PASS or FAIL.

Initial release candidate. Dedicated Gen2+ Shelly Light / RGB / RGBW control over the on-device JSON-RPC 2.0 API (`POST /rpc`) — no Shelly Cloud, no issued credentials. · Full light surface the generic IntegrateIT Shelly driver cannot model: Power On / Off / Toggle, Set Brightness (1-100% with an optional transition), Set Color (RGB 0-255), and Set White Level (0-255) via Light.Set/Toggle, RGB.Set/Toggle, and RGBW.Set/Toggle. One Light / RGB / RGBW component (id 0-3) per instance; the method prefix follows the configured component type. · Real two-way feedback read back from `<Component>.GetStatus`: POWER, BRIGHTNESS (0-100), RGB (`r,g,b`), and WHITE (0-255) — reported by the device, never assumed. The first observed value is absorbed silently (unknown to known fires no events). · State events with exactly-once semantics across duplicate/merged status frames: Turned On / Turned Off, Brightness Changed, and Color Changed (rgb or white) on genuine transitions only. · Component-discovery honesty: Detect Device reads Shelly.GetDeviceInfo (refusing Gen1), then enumerates Shelly.GetComponents and confirms the configured slot exists — refusing an absent component with the mismatch reason and the list of light components the device actually has. · Capability honesty: Set Color is refused locally on a Light component and Set White Level on an RGB (or Light) component, each naming the missing channel in Last Error rather than firing a request the component cannot honor. · Fault reporting (overtemp, overpower, overvoltage, undervoltage, overcurrent) published from the component's errors[] to LAST_ERROR with a Fault Detected event on a fault transition. Tokens are matched on their prefix, so a colon-suffixed detail (overpower:channel_0) still fires with the full string preserved in LAST_ERROR. · Polled status transport (consistent with the shipped IntegrateIT Shelly + Shelly Cover drivers — the Gen2 outbound-WebSocket push is a deliberate v1 non-goal); reachability drives Went Online / Went Offline. Status refreshes tolerate arbitrary junk and odd whitespace around the fields they read. · Gen2+ SHA-256 digest auth gated behind an OS-crypto capability check and verified on hardware — no unexercised hash path ships; a 401 surfaces the hardware gate and the password is never logged (Debug prints method + path only). · LAN-only destination safeguard (private / link-local / *.local, with an explicit Allow Non-LAN Address override); bounded backoff that honors a 429 Retry-After so the driver never hammers a rate-limited device. · MAC-locked IntegrateIT licensing gates every actuating path, checked at command entry and re-checked at the wire-write moment; status polling continues under Strict enforcement. · Simulation-verified via the IntegrateIT driver-factory QA gate; representative Shelly light hardware acceptance is pending.
